findings.text: Locked memory accounting entry accepts a descriptor plus a page count and a direction flag, returning a status code. Empty requests and missing descriptors succeed immediately without further work. Nontrivial requests consult current privilege for interprocess locking and delegate to an internal accounting helper.

User mapping helper accepts file, address, length, protection, flags and byte offset. It rejects requests where aligned length added to offset wraps around, and requests where offset is not page aligned, signalling invalid argument. Valid requests are forwarded with offset expressed as a page number.

Shadow stack allocator creates a readable writable anonymous private region for the current task with shadow stack flavour. A supplied address forces a nonreplacing fixed placement; otherwise placement is free. When transparent huge page support is enabled at build time the region opts out of huge pages. Creation runs under the address space write lock and returns the placed address or an error encoding.

Kernel virtual allocator family provides byte sized, node constrained, range constrained, array and zeroing forms. Array forms multiply count by element size with overflow detection and fail cleanly on overflow. Default forms use kernel reclaimable memory; zeroing forms request cleared pages. Unsupported allocation modifier bits are masked to a supported set with a one time diagnostic.

Commit accounting exposes a limit query and a current usage query. The limit combines swap capacity with either an absolute kilobyte reserve or a percentage of non huge page RAM. Usage is read as the positive sum of a shared per CPU counter.

Overcommit tuning is exposed through a virtual memory control table with entries for policy, ratio, absolute kilobytes and user and administrator reserves. Registration occurs during early initialization. Policy writes are range checked, ratio and absolute forms are mutually clearing, and switching to strict mode refreshes batching and synchronizes counters across processors before publishing the new policy.

Locked accounting and shadow stack creation serialize against concurrent address space changes by holding the address space write lock across their core operation, releasing it before returning status or address.

Small page table installation enables a lazy update mode for the duration of a batch of entry writes and disables it afterwards, marking the table as modified. Descriptor publication orders prior field stores before clearing the uninitialized marker with a write barrier, pairing with read barriers on inspection paths.
Mapping requests fail when the sum of offset and aligned length is numerically smaller than offset, indicating wrap, and when offset has subpage bits set. No mapping attempt occurs in those cases.

Shadow stack regions always carry anonymous private semantics and read plus write access. Fixed placement is used exactly when the caller supplies a nonzero address, with replacement forbidden. Huge page use is disabled whenever the corresponding build option is present.

Range allocation rejects empty sizes and sizes whose page count exceeds total physical pages, reporting failure without reserving an area. Caller allocation modifiers outside the supported virtual allocation set are reduced to that set before proceeding.

Backing store setup derives a small page count from the reserved span and sizes a pointer array accordingly. Arrays larger than one page come from the virtual allocator itself with zeroed reclaimable modifiers; smaller arrays come from the slab allocator on the requested node. High memory is permitted unless device memory was requested. Failure to obtain the array aborts the request through deferred cleanup.

Page range installation requires each target entry to be currently empty, each supplied page pointer to be present, and each frame number to be valid; violations abort the batch with distinct error encodings for busy, out of memory and invalid argument. Requested mapping granularity must be at least the base page size. Kernel table synchronization is performed only when the walk marked modifications requiring it.

Physical page fulfilment first attempts large power of two blocks without direct reclaim, decreasing the attempt size on failure and splitting successful blocks into individual entries. Order zero remainders use a bulk path in bounded chunks with memory policy awareness, falling back to single page allocation. Loops stop early on pending fatal signals unless no fail semantics were requested, and every obtained page is accounted to virtual allocation usage.

Allocation modifiers gain a suppression of allocation warnings, and large requests shed no fail semantics. No fail handling is disabled entirely when the caller context forbids blocking. Page table installation runs under a restricted allocation scope derived from caller reclaim, filesystem and input output permissions, restored afterwards.

Successful writes to the ratio control clear the absolute kilobyte control and vice versa, so at most one shapes the limit. Policy changes recompute batching first, then synchronize the committed counter on every processor when entering strict mode, and only then publish the policy value, limiting skew and races.

When an absolute kilobyte reserve is configured it is converted to pages and used directly; otherwise the allowance is total RAM minus huge table pages scaled by the configured percentage. Swap capacity is always added. Committed usage never reports negative values.

Range allocation proceeds from reservation through backing store acquisition and table installation to sanitizer handling, publication and leak tracking. Huge granularity is attempted first when permitted and supported; any reservation or mapping failure at large granularity retries at base granularity. No fail reservations retry indefinitely with a brief sleep. Publication clears the uninitialized marker and records the area unless deferred tracking was requested.

Kernel range installation descends through successive table levels from top to leaf, allocating missing intermediate tables as needed and propagating allocation failures upward as out of memory. Leaf batches install entries sequentially while advancing a shared index. Large granularities iterate stride by stride with physical continuity; small granularities use a dedicated leaf walker. Cache maintenance follows successful installation.

Arithmetic hazards include offset plus length wrap, subpage offsets, and count times size overflow in array helpers; all are rejected with failure encodings rather than truncated. Sizing hazards include empty requests and requests exceeding total RAM. Installation hazards include occupied entries, missing pages and invalid frames, each aborting the batch. Page array, page supply and table build failures all lead to cleanup without leaking a half built area.

No fail semantics introduce unbounded retry with voluntary sleeps when reservation or table build fails, and high order no fail page requests are especially costly. To avoid blocking or recursion hazards, failures in backing store acquisition and mapping divert the descriptor to asynchronous cleanup via a pending list and scheduled work rather than freeing inline.

Virtual area descriptors observed here carry a base address, a pointer array for backing pages, a count of present pages, a page order for the mapping granularity, a flags word including allocation, uninitialized and huge related bits, a caller address for tracking, and a list node for deferred cleanup. Order storage is architecture gated and must be zero where huge virtual mappings are unsupported.

Default tuning values are guess mode for overcommit policy, fifty percent for overcommit ratio, zero absolute kilobytes meaning ratio mode, a standard maximum map count, one hundred twenty eight megabytes user reserve and eight megabytes administrator reserve.

Bulk zero order fulfilment caps each request at one hundred pages to bound disabled preemption intervals. Range allocation spans from the virtual allocation start to its end with base page alignment, and huge attempts use progressively larger granularities before falling back to base size.
